title: Right Kan extension from the zeroth simplex gives finite powers
statement: Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], cocartesian fibrations and cocartesian-edge-preserving functors of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and cocartesian straightening of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. Let $i:\{[0]\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ be the inclusion of the zeroth simplex. Evaluation $i^*:\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Cat}_\infty)\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ has a right adjoint $i_*$ given by right Kan extension. For every small infinity category $C$, $(i_*C)_{[n]}=C^{n+1}$; a map $[m]\to[n]$ in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, opposite to a monotone $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$, acts by $(c_j)_{j\in[m]}\mapsto(c_{\alpha(i)})_{i\in[n]}$, so the elementary faces are projections and degeneracies are diagonals; in particular the transport along the arrow $[n]\to[0]$ opposite to the vertex $j:[0]\to[n]$ is the $j$th coordinate projection $C^{n+1}\to C$. Under straightening, $i_*C$ is represented by the cocartesian fibration $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_C\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. For every cocartesian fibration $q:E\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, the adjunction gives a natural equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{/\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}(E,\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_C)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cat}_\infty}(E_{[0]},C)$ between maps over the base preserving cocartesian edges and maps from the zeroth fibre, given by restriction to the fibres over $[0]$ (using $(i_*C)_{[0]}=C$); this equivalence is natural in $C$ and $q$.

source.place: Definition 4.1.1, Remark 4.1.2, Remark 4.1.5 and Proposition 4.2.3(iii) (pp. 36-37 of the arXiv PDF): i_* right adjoint to the fibre-at-[0] functor i^*, the finite-power formula, and the comparison map obtained from the adjunction.

proof.text: Write $J=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ and let $A=\{[0]\}\subseteq J$. This is a full subcategory: the only endomorphism of $[0]$ is the identity. For a vertex $[n]$ of $J$, the coslice $L_n=A\times_J J_{[n]/}$ is discrete with objects the arrows $\rho_j:[n]\to[0]$, $0\leq j\leq n$. Indeed such an arrow is opposite to a monotone map $[0]\to[n]$, hence a choice of vertex $j$; a simplex whose entire tail lies in $A$ has all tail arrows identities, so it is a degeneracy of that chosen arrow. Consequently, for $h:A\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ with value $C$, the diagram $h|_{L_n}$ is the constant $n+1$-term discrete diagram. The finite-product clause of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] supplies its limit $P_n=C^{n+1}$ with the coordinate projections. In mapping-space form this says $\operatorname{Map}(T,P_n)\simeq\prod_{j=0}^n\operatorname{Map}(T,C)$. Apply the dual constant-source test in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test] to $p:\operatorname{Cat}_\infty\to *$: both lower mapping spaces in its square are points, so the product cone is exactly the required $p$-limit lift over the unique base cone. All $L_n$ and their cones are small in the fixed input universe. At $n=0$ this is the one-factor cone $C\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}C$.

source.place: Definition 4.1.1 and Remark 4.1.2: calculation of the right-Kan indexing categories and their product limits.

proof.text: Apply the right-hand dual of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-kan-existence] with full subcategory $A\subseteq J$, $\mathcal D=\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$, $\mathcal B=*$, $s:J\to *$ the unique diagram and $h([0])=C$. The map $p:\mathcal D\to *$ is an isofibration: its inner lifting problems are those of the quasicategory $\mathcal D$, and the only base equivalence lifts by an identity. Step 1 provides all its prescribed local $p$-limit lifts, including the cone at $[0]$. Thus there is a coherent functor $G_C:J\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ with $G_C|_A=h$ exactly and whose canonical cones on every $L_n$ are limiting. No assertion that products alone automatically specify a coherent diagram is used. These are precisely pointwise right Kan extensions along $i$, and the limiting cones identify $G_C([n])$ with $C^{n+1}$ together with every projection $G_C(\rho_j)$. Only these finite products are needed, rather than arbitrary large limits in $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$.

source.place: Definition 4.1.1, expanded using the existing right-hand relative Kan-existence theorem.

proof.text:
For any coherent $F:J\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$, apply [lem-coef-infinity-kan-mapping-restriction] with full subcategory $A\subseteq J$, source $F$ and target $G_C$. Its right-Kan hypothesis is exactly the limit-cone property obtained in step 2. It gives restriction itself as a natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Cat}_\infty)}(F,G_C)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,\operatorname{Cat}_\infty)}(F|_A,h)=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cat}_\infty}(F([0]),C).$$
The final identification follows from $A=\Delta^0$: an $r$-simplex of its functor category is simply an $r$-simplex of the target. Hence for each $C$, the presheaf $F\mapsto\operatorname{Map}(i^*F,C)$ is represented by $G_C$. The existing pointwise-adjoint criterion [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-adjoint-criterion] assembles these representing objects and the representing maps to a coherent right adjoint $i_*$, with the displayed natural equivalence as adjunction. Use these restriction equivalences as the representing data and choose the representatives $i_*C=G_C$. The counit at $C$ is the image of $1_{G_C}$ under the displayed equivalence; restriction sends it to $1_{G_C|_A}=1_C$, so the counit $i^*i_*C\to C$ is the identity under the fixed boundary identification. The criterion may be applied in larger fixed universes containing $J$, $\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}$ and its functor category and all their mapping spaces; this changes neither the $\mathcal U$-small objects $G_C([n])$ nor the small total fibrations. The comparison is natural in both $F$ and $C$, with transformations and all higher parameter simplices retained.

source.place: Remark 4.1.5 and Proposition 4.2.3(3): right adjoint to fibre-at-[0], with its full mapping-space universal property.

proof.text:
Let $\beta:[m]\to[n]$ in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ be opposite to $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$. Precomposition sends the vertex $\rho_i^n:[n]\to[0]$ to $\rho_i^n\beta=\rho_{\alpha(i)}^m:[m]\to[0]$. The limiting cones of step 2 therefore give
$$\operatorname{pr}_i\,G_C(\beta)\simeq G_C(\rho_i^n\beta)=\operatorname{pr}_{\alpha(i)}.$$
The universal property of the target product identifies this functor with $(c_j)_{j\in[m]}\mapsto(c_{\alpha(i)})_{i\in[n]}$, on objects and every mapping simplex. For the identity base arrow each coordinate is unchanged. If $\beta':[n]\to[r]$ is opposite to $\gamma:[r]\to[n]$, then the $k$th coordinate of $G_C(\beta')G_C(\beta)$ is the $\gamma(k)$th coordinate after $G_C(\beta)$, hence the original $\alpha(\gamma(k))$th coordinate. This is exactly the coordinate for $\beta'\beta$, opposite to $\alpha\circ\gamma:[r]\to[m]$; the already constructed coherent functor and its cones supply the higher compatibilities. The elementary faces omit a coordinate and the degeneracies repeat one. In particular transport along $\rho_j$ is the $j$th projection and at $[0]$ the one-factor product is $C$. The displayed equality $(i_*C)_{[n]}=C^{n+1}$ uses these specified product identifications; no strict equality of arbitrary choices of limits is asserted.

source.place: Remark 4.1.2: explicit projections, diagonals and the vertex projection formula.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], $i_*C$ is classified by a cocartesian fibration $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_C\to J$. For any $q:E\to J$, the same equivalence takes $q$ to its coherent fibre diagram $F=\operatorname{St}_J(q)$, with $F([0])=E_{[0]}$, and takes cocartesian-edge-preserving maps over $J$ to transformations of these diagrams. It therefore identifies the mapping space of such maps $E\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_C$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Cat}_\infty)}(F,i_*C)$. Step 3 identifies the latter with $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cat}_\infty}(E_{[0]},C)$. Straightening commutes coherently with base restriction, in particular with $\{[0]\}\to J$; since the counit of step 3 is the identity on $C$, this composite equivalence is exactly restriction to the zeroth fibres. The fibre and edge-preservation conventions are those of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Finally the straightening and adjunction equivalences are natural, so this restriction equivalence is natural in $q$ and $C$, not merely a bijection of homotopy classes. Size: [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] is stated for $\mathcal U$-small total categories. If $E$ is only $\mathcal U'$-small, run steps 1--5 verbatim with $\mathcal U'$ in place of $\mathcal U$ (and a larger universe in place of $\mathcal U'$): $C$ is also $\mathcal U'$-small, the inclusion $\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}\subseteq\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U'}$ is fully faithful and preserves the finite products $C^{n+1}$ of step 1 (the product mapping property of step 1 holds for every test object $T$ of the larger category, since $\operatorname{Map}(T,C^{n+1})$ is computed coordinatewise), so the same $G_C$ is the right Kan extension in either universe, and the resulting restriction equivalence is the stated one.
